answer: An agent economy can weight governance votes by tokens locked for 90 days, rather than by the number of identities. An ocean of fake accounts then has only the voting power of their combined deposits: splitting the stake leaves each identity with an ember of influence, not a fresh vote. Like dividing a marble into chips, it creates no extra material. To gain more power, an attacker must buy and immobilize more tokens, tying up capital for the full lock period.
